faq.q: What is the best boat for Ironman recovery in Marbella?
faq.a: For a small group, the Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39 (both 12.5m, up to 11 guests) are ideal. They offer comfortable seating and shade, perfect for post-race relaxation. Prices start at €749 for 2 hours.

faq.q: Can I charter a boat for just a few hours after the race?
faq.a: Yes. Our Tier A boats are available from 2 hours (€749). For longer recovery, 4- or 8-hour charters let you explore the coast at a gentle pace.

faq.q: What is included in the charter price?
faq.a: Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). No hidden costs.

faq.q: Do you offer larger yachts for bigger groups?

faq.q: Where do the boats depart from?
faq.a: All our boats depart from Puerto Banús, Marbella. It is a 10-minute drive from the Ironman finish area, with easy parking and taxi access.

faq.q: Can I bring my own food or recovery drinks?
faq.a: We provide light snacks and drinks, but you are welcome to bring your own food. Our skipper can also recommend catering options for a fee.

faq.q: What if the weather is bad on race day?
faq.a: We monitor forecasts closely. If conditions are unsafe, we offer a full refund or reschedule to the next available day. Your safety is our priority.

faq.q: How do I book a recovery charter?
faq.a: Contact us via WhatsApp for availability and pricing. We recommend booking at least 2 weeks in advance for Ironman weekend, as slots fill quickly.

data.body_html:
Crossing the finish line of Ironman 2036 in Marbella is a monumental achievement. After 3.8 km of swimming, 180 km of cycling, and 42.2 km of running, your body deserves more than a cold beer on a sun lounger. A Marbella boat rental for Ironman 2036 recovery offers the perfect blend of relaxation, gentle movement, and stunning coastal views. Charter a private yacht from Puerto Banús, let our skipper handle the navigation, and spend the day floating on the Mediterranean with your support crew.

Why a boat charter beats a hotel pool for recovery

Active recovery—light movement in a cool environment—helps flush lactic acid and reduce muscle soreness. A boat provides a low-impact setting: you can stretch on the deck, swim in the sea (water temperature in October averages 21 °C), or simply lie in the shade. Unlike a crowded hotel pool, you control the pace. Our Tier A boats, such as the Astondoa 40 (12.5 m, 9 guests), start at €749 for 2 hours, including skipper, drinks, and snacks. No rushing, no queues.

Our fleet: boats suited for post-race relaxation

We operate from Puerto Banús with a range of yachts. For small groups (up to 5 guests), the Dubhe (8 m) or Mariah SX21 (6.4 m) offer intimate charters. For larger parties (up to 12 guests), consider the Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6 m) or the Mangusta 80 (24 m, from €4,719 for 4 hours with a free jet ski). All boats include a licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, and Spanish IVA. See the full list on our boat rental hub.

Where to cruise: calm spots near Marbella

Your skipper will recommend routes based on sea conditions and your energy levels. Popular recovery itineraries include:

  • Marbella Marina to Cabopino – 5 NM east, sheltered coves like Cala del Faro for a gentle swim.
  • Puerto Banús to Estepona – 8 NM west, passing the Golden Mile and Río Verde. Calm waters, dolphin sightings common.
  • Sotogrande loop – 15 NM south, for a longer cruise with lunch at a beach club.

Each route takes 2–4 hours, leaving plenty of time for rest.

How to book your recovery charter

Demand is high during Ironman weekend. To secure your preferred boat, contact us via WhatsApp at least two weeks in advance. Provide your group size, preferred date and time, and any special requests (e.g., catering, extra towels). We will confirm availability and send a booking link. For pricing on larger yachts like the Ferretti 94 (29 m, 12 guests), message us directly.

What to bring for optimal recovery

Pack light: swimwear, a towel, sunscreen (reef-safe), a hat, and compression gear if you plan to swim. We provide cold drinks and snacks, but you are welcome to bring your own electrolyte drinks or protein bars. The boat has a shaded saloon and a sun pad—perfect for a post-race nap.
